title: From an inference result to a grain plan
text: agronomist closing season three inference results waiting desk – nitrogen-response trial, variety trial, protein target – one blunt question : actually , tell tool trust evidence enough answer? wrong number costs season’s margin; confident wrong number worse plain shrug, nobody double-checks number looks sure . grainPlan practitioner last-mile ORCHESTRA agricultural analytics stack. upstream member produces inference result – yield posterior, multi-environment variety trial, genomic prediction – grainPlan turns actionable grain-production plan: much nitrogen apply, variety sow, whether chase quality grade. thin grain-semantics layer decideR decision engine: expected-utility maximisation, abstention logic, grounding firewall decideR’s, reused whole; grainPlan adds grain economics grain meaning. walkthrough runs end--end real public data agridat package answers agronomist’s question three times – rate, variety, grade target – fourth time case report afford get wrong: plan looks like one legs trust.

title: From an inference result to a grain plan

Every one wraps decideR::decide() sibling engine call returns grain_decision: recommended action, unit, grower-facing rationale, grounding token copied straight wrapped decideR::decision, never recomputed. plan_season() gathers several grain_decisions one grain_plan, combining grounding worst-case decideR::combine_grounding() plan resting unverified decision unverified; grain_plan_table() flattens plan one-row-per-decision table report reads, grain_is_grounded() predicate downstream automation gates acting. grain value library – wheat_protein_bands(), barley_malting_premium(), n_rate_economics() – consolidates economics decisions price , schedule named documented rather anonymous expression re-derived every call site.

what: A nitrogen rate from a real yield response
title: From an inference result to a grain plan
text: agridat dataset lasrosas.corn records corn yield-monitor data field near Las Rosas, Rio Cuarto, Cordoba, Argentina, variable nitrogen fertiliser across 1999 2001 harvests (Anselin, Bongiovanni & Lowenberg-DeBoer, 2004). summarise yield-response curve, build posterior yield candidate rate, ask grainPlan profit-optimal rate. economics live grain value library: n_rate_economics() consolidates profit utility – revenue grain price less nitrogen cost – profit-priced rate decision reads economics rather anonymous expression. recommendation grain_decision: chosen rate, crop, grower-facing rationale, – carried beside numbers, never inferred – grounding token. Expected profit candidate nitrogen rate lasrosas.corn fit: profit rises status quo, peaks chosen rate, falls away beyond . curve decision decisive rather coin toss neighbouring rates: expected profit rises steadily status quo, peaks sharply chosen rate, falls away either side , gap chosen rate nearest neighbours well posterior’s rate--rate noise.
code: data("lasrosas.corn", package = "agridat") corn <- lasrosas.corn  # A candidate nitrogen grid spanning the trial, and a simple yield-response # summary: a quadratic mean-yield fit against nitrogen, with the trial's # residual spread used to build a posterior of yield at each rate. This # stands in for the yield posterior an ORCHESTRA inference member (a PESTO # inversion, a mechanistic yield-response model) would emit as an # orchestra_manifest. # # The draws MUST be coupled across rate columns: one draw index has to mean # "the same realised season" at every candidate rate, because the decision # is a paired comparison between candidate rates on the posterior, not a # comparison of two independent samples. We therefore draw one residual # vector `eps` and add it to every rate's fitted mean, rather than drawing # each column independently (independent columns roughly double the # between-rate contrast variance and can mask a real, decisive difference). rates <- seq(0, 120, by = 20) fit <- stats::lm(yield ~ nitro + I(nitro^2), data = corn) sigma <- summary(fit)$sigma  n_draws <- 1500L eps <- stats::rnorm(n_draws, 0, sigma) yield_draws <- vapply(   rates,   function(r) {     mu <- stats::predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(nitro = r))     mu + eps   },   numeric(n_draws))  # Grain and nitrogen prices are the caller's to supply. `lasrosas.corn` # reports yield in quintals/ha (agridat's own documentation), so the grain # price below is expressed per quintal; it is illustrative, not the price # structure the trial's own economic analyses used (Anselin et al. (2004) # report $6.85/quintal and $0.4348/kg N for their own analysis). n_plan <- plan_nitrogen_rate(   yield_draws, rates,   price_grain = 22,             # $ per quintal (illustrative)   price_n = 1.2,                # $ per unit nitrogen (illustrative)   crop = "corn",   grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded())  n_plan #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : corn #>   kind   : nitrogen_rate #>   action : 80 kg N/ha #>   why    : Apply 80 kg N/ha to the corn crop: it maximises expected profit ($1478.3/unit area) and clearly beats the status quo on the posterior. plot_df <- n_plan@decision@candidates plot_df$role <- "candidate" plot_df$role[plot_df$action == 0] <- "status quo" plot_df$role[plot_df$action == n_plan@action] <- "chosen rate" plot_df$role <- factor(plot_df$role,                        levels = c("candidate", "status quo", "chosen rate"))  ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = action, y = expected_utility)) +   ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "grey50") +   ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +   ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(     name = NULL,     values = c(candidate = "#000000", `status quo` = "#0072B2",                `chosen rate` = "#D55E00")) +   ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(     name = NULL,     values = c(candidate = 16, `status quo` = 15, `chosen rate` = 17)) +   ggplot2::labs(     x = "Nitrogen rate (kg N/ha)", y = "Expected profit ($/unit area)",     title = "Profit-vs-rate curve behind the recommendation") +   ggplot2::theme_minimal()

what: A variety choice from a multi-environment trial
title: From an inference result to a grain plan
text: agridat dataset besag.met multi-environment trial 64 corn hybrids across six counties North Carolina, three replicates (Besag & Higdon, 1999). summarise hybrid’s mean performance across counties posterior merit, ask grainPlan rank downside-aware loss – one discounts high-yielding volatile hybrid steady one, stability grower wants sown variety. recommendation leading hybrid downside-aware ranking; full ranked short-list wrapped decision’s candidate ledger, hybrid labels attached (ledger’s action column carries integer index grainPlan decides , join hybrid names back readable table): five leading corn hybrids downside-aware merit ranking.
code: data("besag.met", package = "agridat") met <- besag.met  # Hybrid means across counties, with the county-to-county spread giving each # hybrid a merit posterior. (A factor-analytic MET model -- # flexyBayes -- would emit this directly as an orchestra_manifest; # here we build it directly from the public trial.) The posterior we need # is of the HYBRID MEAN, not of a single plot, so the per-hybrid plot-level # spread must be divided down to a standard error of the mean # (sd / sqrt(n)); using the raw plot-level sd would overstate the mean's # uncertainty by roughly sqrt(n) and could mask a real, decisive ranking. # The trial ships with 36 filler rows (six per county) carrying a missing # yield -- agridat's own note explains they complete the field rectangle for # a spatial model and were never harvested -- so we summarise with na.rm and # fall back to the trial-wide spread (also converted to a standard error) # for any hybrid with too few records to estimate its own. gen_means <- tapply(met$yield, met$gen, mean, na.rm = TRUE) gen_sd <- tapply(met$yield, met$gen, stats::sd, na.rm = TRUE) gen_n <- tapply(met$yield, met$gen, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))) pooled_sd <- stats::sd(met$yield, na.rm = TRUE) gen_sd[is.na(gen_sd)] <- pooled_sd gen_n[gen_n < 2L] <- 1L gen_se <- gen_sd / sqrt(gen_n) varieties <- names(gen_means)  merit_draws <- vapply(   seq_along(gen_means),   function(j) stats::rnorm(1000L, gen_means[j], gen_se[j]),   numeric(1000L)) colnames(merit_draws) <- varieties  v_plan <- plan_variety(   merit_draws, varieties, risk_aversion = 0.5, crop = "corn",   grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded())  v_plan #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : corn #>   kind   : variety #>   action : G05 variety #>   why    : Sow G05 in the corn crop: it leads the downside-aware merit ranking and clearly beats the incumbent (G01) on the posterior. ledger <- v_plan@decision@candidates ledger$hybrid <- varieties[ledger$action] ledger <- ledger[order(-ledger$expected_utility),                  c("hybrid", "action", "expected_utility", "feasible")]

title: From an inference result to a grain plan
text: Many grain payoffs smooth outcome reward: delivery paid quality grade, value steps protein threshold rather rising continuously. grainPlan’s value library consolidates grade schedules. wheat_protein_bands() prices Australian milling-wheat grades protein, following band thresholds published Grain Trade Australia, plan_grade_target() decides hard push protein-driving input step payoff – decision governed posterior probability clearing band, exactly threshold economics decideR’s grade-band loss expresses. Wheat protein-band payoffs (wheat_protein_bands() defaults; dollar values illustrative, band shape follows Grain Trade Australia’s published thresholds). wheat protein-band value schedule (wheat_protein_bands()): price per tonne steps published grade threshold. Dashed lines mark milling/hard/prime-hard breaks; step shape table show. baseline protein posterior just milling band, nitrogen top-lifts protein per-unit cost, gives grainPlan something weigh schedule: decision prices chance clearing 11.5% band cost pushing . cost top-pays : recommended input level top candidate range, expected graded payoff rises monotonically higher probability clearing 11.5% band – candidate ledger shows full trade-. Full candidate ledger behind grade-target recommendation.
code: protein_value <- wheat_protein_bands() grid_protein <- seq(9, 14, by = 0.02) schedule_df <- data.frame(   protein = grid_protein,   payoff = protein_value(grid_protein)) breaks_df <- data.frame(protein = attr(protein_value, "breaks"))  ggplot2::ggplot(schedule_df, ggplot2::aes(x = protein, y = payoff)) +   ggplot2::geom_step(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.9) +   ggplot2::geom_vline(data = breaks_df, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = protein),                        linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +   ggplot2::labs(     x = "Grain protein (%)", y = "Payoff ($/tonne)",     title = "Wheat protein-band value schedule") +   ggplot2::theme_minimal() protein <- stats::rnorm(2000L, mean = 11.0, sd = 0.5) g_plan <- plan_grade_target(   protein, actions = seq(0, 60, by = 10), value = protein_value,   quality_shift = function(rate, p) p + 0.02 * rate, cost = 0.3,   crop = "wheat", grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded())  g_plan #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : wheat #>   kind   : grade_target #>   action : 60 input level #>   why    : Set the input to 60 for the wheat crop: it maximises the expected graded payoff ($341.41/t) by raising the posterior probability of clearing a higher quality band, net of input cost.

text: examples far assembled yield merit posteriors hand. orchestra, upstream member emits orchestra_manifest instead – C2 v2 generic manifest contract orchestra’s cross-package governance – grainPlan reads directly decideR’s duck-typed pipeline tail, taking dependency manifest constructor package. minimal stand-built tiny S7 class, standing manifest real producer emit. yield-per-rate draws matrix, shape PESTO inversion emits, carried outputs producer’s grounding token metadata$grounding: genomic tail reads breeding values way. breeding_values manifest carries point GEBVs outputs$gebv alongside genomic uncertainty, reconstruction uses genotypes’ reliability rather invented spread. point-GEBV manifest carries uncertainty gebv_sd supplied, grainPlan stops rather fabricate scale reconstruction: genotype switch must turn magic constant. stop bug route around: firewall discipline grounding token, applied different way upstream producer’s claim can thin act . manifest can also carry refusal . upstream producer declares, summary slot, produce usable result – PESTO ensemble never converged, say – grainPlan reads typed abstention ever looks draws, holds decision status quo regardless (declined) manifest happens carry: Note producer’s grounding token claimed grounded; grainPlan never reaches , typed abstention checked first. returned object also carries class stamp fleet-level gate can read without knowing came grainPlan specifically: grainPlan_abstention orchestra_refusal prepended ahead grainPlan::grain_decision, naming convention orchestra’s cross-member decline gate reads producer-agnostically – downstream automation recognises refused decision without special-casing grainPlan’s class.
code: mini_manifest <- S7::new_class(   "mini_manifest",   properties = list(     outputs         = S7::class_any,     metadata        = S7::class_list,     run_id          = S7::class_character,     emitter_package = S7::class_character)) rates_m <- seq(0, 150, by = 25) ymax    <- stats::rnorm(1200L, 5.5, 0.3) yld_m   <- vapply(rates_m,                   function(r) 3 + (ymax - 3) * (1 - exp(-r / 80)),                   numeric(1200L)) ym <- mini_manifest(outputs = yld_m,                     metadata = list(grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded()))  plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest(ym, rates_m, price_grain = 350, price_n = 1.3,                                  crop = "wheat") #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : wheat #>   kind   : nitrogen_rate #>   action : 150 kg N/ha #>   why    : Apply 150 kg N/ha to the wheat crop: it maximises expected profit ($1593/unit area) and clearly beats the status quo on the posterior. gm <- mini_manifest(   outputs  = list(gebv = c(Scepter = 0.2, Vixen = 1.1, Calibre = -0.3),                   pev  = c(0.04, 0.04, 0.04)),   metadata = list(grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded()))  g_dec <- plan_variety_from_manifest(gm, risk_aversion = 0.5) g_dec #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : wheat #>   kind   : variety #>   action : Vixen variety #>   why    : Sow Vixen in the wheat crop: it leads the downside-aware merit ranking and clearly beats the incumbent (Scepter) on the posterior. g_dec@context$gebv_sd_source #> [1] "manifest_pev" gm_no_sd <- mini_manifest(   outputs  = list(gebv = c(Scepter = 0.2, Vixen = 1.1, Calibre = -0.3)),   metadata = list(grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded()))  plan_variety_from_manifest(gm_no_sd, risk_aversion = 0.5) #> Error: #> ! manifest carries point GEBVs with no per-genotype uncertainty (`pev`, `gebv_se`, or `reliability` + `genetic_var`) and `gebv_sd` was not supplied. Pass `gebv_sd` on the GEBV scale, or provide a manifest that carries the genomic uncertainty -- grainPlan will not fabricate it. refused_manifest <- mini_manifest(   outputs = list(),   metadata = list(     grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded(),     summary = list(headline = "no stable fit found", abstained = TRUE)),   run_id = "demo-refused-01", emitter_package = "PESTO")  gd_refused <- plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest(   refused_manifest, rates_m, price_grain = 350, price_n = 1.3, crop = "corn")  gd_refused #> <grain_decision> ABSTAINED  [ungrounded] #>   crop   : corn #>   kind   : nitrogen_rate #>   action : 0 kg N/ha #>   why    : Held at the status-quo rate: the upstream evidence producer itself declined to produce a result, so the recommendation is withheld. class(gd_refused) #> [1] "orchestra_refusal"         "grainPlan_abstention"      #> [3] "grainPlan::grain_decision" "S7_object"

Every recommendation plan carries grounding, plan whole carries worst case – grower, downstream automation, can gate grain_is_grounded() acting. decisions grounded, plan reads clean end end. easy case. harder, consequential case happens one leg season inherits refusal upstream – gd_refused decision built two sections back, standing PESTO ensemble never converged. code: season <- plan_season(   list(v_plan, n_plan),   crop = "corn", season = "2026 demonstration")  season #> <grain_plan> 2026 demonstration -- 2 decisions  [grounded] #>   - [decide  ] variety       : G05 variety #>   - [decide  ] nitrogen_rate : 80 kg N/ha season_tbl <- grain_plan_table(season) grain_is_grounded(season) #> [1] TRUE season_refusal <- plan_season(   list(v_plan, gd_refused),   crop = "corn",   season = "2026 demonstration -- nitrogen evidence withheld upstream")  season_refusal #> <grain_plan> 2026 demonstration -- nitrogen evidence withheld upstream -- 2 decisions  [ungrounded]  (partial abstention) #>   - [decide  ] variety       : G05 variety #>   - [ABSTAIN ] nitrogen_rate : 0 kg N/ha refusal_tbl <- grain_plan_table(season_refusal) grain_is_grounded(season_refusal) #> [1] FALSE

title: Print a grain decision — print.grain_decision
code: set.seed(1L) rates <- seq(0, 150, by = 25) ymax  <- rnorm(800L, 5.5, 0.3) yld   <- vapply(rates, function(r) 3 + (ymax - 3) * (1 - exp(-r / 70)),                 numeric(800L)) print(plan_nitrogen_rate(yld, rates, price_grain = 350, price_n = 1.3,                          crop = "wheat",                          grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded())) #> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded] #>   crop   : wheat #>   kind   : nitrogen_rate #>   action : 150 kg N/ha #>   why    : Apply 150 kg N/ha to the wheat crop: it maximises expected profit ($1625.8/unit area) and clearly beats the status quo on the posterior.

Repriced $22/quintal; example now recommends non-zero rate new captioned figure shows profit-vs-rate curve behind (GP-15, GP-16). variety-ranking vignette chunk used genotype’s plot-level residual spread posterior standard deviation genotype mean, overstates uncertainty roughly square root replicate count; corrected standard error mean (sd / sqrt(n)). prose claiming “recommendation leading genotype” now consistent printed decision, previously abstained (GP-07). variety short-list ledger printed integer candidate indices genotype label; vignette now joins variety names back onto ledger printing (GP-08). Printing decideR::grade_band_value schedule dumped closure body run-specific memory address rendered vignette; now rendered breaks/values/labels attributes (GP-14). grade-target example’s cost high enough relative quality shift profit-optimal action degenerated status quo, point printed rationale (“raising posterior probability clearing higher quality band”) describe zero-input action ; example cost lowered demonstration reaches genuine, non-degenerate recommendation, full candidate ledger now shown. Minor grammar naming fixes: “nitrogen response trial” hyphenated “nitrogen-response trial”; lasrosas.corn trial location corrected “Las Rosas” (agridat’s spelling), vignette’s prior “Lasrosas farm”. README.Rmd now renders without pandoc smart-punctuation substitution (md_extensions: -smart), README.md longer carries Unicode en dashes prose; regenerated. vignette restructured orchestra’s vignette quality bar: stated grower question front, fixed ///Read/Limits/-- read-next/Reproduce shape, two ggplot2 figures (profit-vs-rate curve wheat protein-band schedule) replacing base-graphics plot raw attribute dump, every table knitr::kable(), new season-composition example showing plan inherits upstream manifest producer’s typed abstention alongside grounded decision, read plan’s grain_plan_table() grain_is_grounded() output. besag.met variety example now labelled crop = "corn" (trial 64 corn hybrids across six North Carolina counties, wheat); citations added agridat sources (Anselin, Bongiovanni & Lowenberg-DeBoer, 2004; Besag & Higdon, 1999).

title: grainPlan 0.1.0
text: Grain decision verbs wrap decideR’s engine grain meaning: plan_nitrogen_rate() plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest() price nitrogen rate expected profit; plan_variety() plan_variety_from_manifest() rank variety multi-environment trial breeding_values manifest downside-aware merit loss; plan_grade_target() chooses quality-driving input grade-band payoff. reusable grain value / loss library consolidates economics orchestra runs kept hand-building: wheat_protein_bands(), barley_malting_premium() (decideR::grade_band_value() schedules built published grade conventions), n_rate_economics(). season orchestrator: plan_season() composes several grain decisions one grain_plan, combining grounding worst-case plan resting unverified decision abstains whole; grain_plan_table() flattens plan report. S7 result types grain_decision (one recommended grain action wrapping decideR::decision) grain_plan (ordered season decisions), grain_is_grounded() predicate print() methods. Independent Oracle Principle firewall inherited enforced every verb: ungrounded input forces abstention status quo, never confident wrong recommendation.
